items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: No direct interaction or personal relationship described between Gil Evans and Pastor John Gensel in the transcript.

ctx.x: Endowment for the Arts in Washington. As a matter of fact, it is one of their projects and has been administered by the Jazz Interaction in New York for which Lois McCloud is the project coordinator.

The whole project has been developed in cooperation with Pastor John Gensel known affectionately and wisely in New York as the priest to the jazz community. He is an associate pastor at St. Peter's Lutheran Church. And is very, very well known for his jazz projects.

Now, I'd like to quote finally from Ralph Gleason and this is on the back of the Ampex Album. He says, the thing that in a sense marks Gil Evan's work, and I'm changing the words around just a little bit here, is that he stays contemporary as do Ellington and Miles. And he draws from what is going on around him, absorbs it, digests it and when he is ready to appear again utilises it all in a new way.
